subject: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kira Dawson <kira@optiscale.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift

Hi Kira —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As OptiScale approaches renewals, we wanted to put a concise set of options on the table so you can take them to procurement. High-level ask from your side was: premium SLA (lower tail latency SLOs), dedicated burst capacity during peak launches, and clearer crediting for incidents.

Attached: redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf (summary of options) and a draft MPA with redlines flagged. Quick summary of the three viable upgrade tracks:

- Essentials Uplift (12mo): 99th percentile request latency target reduction from 450ms -> 300ms for gen workloads; includes standard support hours and one prioritized onboarding sprint.
- Premium Response (12mo + commit): 99.9th percentile tail latency target band, 24/7 priority support, 8 hours P1 response SLA, and 200% burst pool for incident mitigation. Pricing includes a 12-month commit discount tier.
- Enterprise Reserved (24mo): Premium Response plus guaranteed reserved GPUs for sustained peak windows, quarterly performance reviews, and a small ops runbook workshop.

We proposed two commercial levers to help close: a one-time credit for historical incident exposure (applied as billing credit) and a limited run of free burst credits for the first 90 days of the renewed term so you can validate the new SLOs in production without immediate spend.

Would you and your procurement partner be available for a 30-minute alignment call on Monday (5/17) or Tuesday (5/18)? If you like, I can include our CS lead and product ops to walk the proposed guardrails (circuit-breakers, canary rollout cadence, and a rollback policy).

Attachments:
- redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf (2 pages)
- draft_mpa_redlines.docx (tracked changes)

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Kira Dawson <kira@optiscale.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@optiscale.com>
Date: 2027-05-12T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift

Jordan —

Appreciate the summary and the proposal doc. A few rapid clarifications so I can scope procurement:

1) Can you break down the price delta between Essentials Uplift and Premium Response as a per-token / per-hour equivalent? We need an apples-to-apples run-rate for our FinOps team.
2) For the burst credits you propose: what are the hard limits (tokens/hour and time window) and how do they auto-expire?
3) Incident crediting: procurement wants a formulaic credit calculation tied to downtime/latency breach windows rather than an opaque one-off. Can you propose a simple formula we can include in the MPA?

Jason is on copy — he'll be the primary contact for contract language and will want to see the MPA redlines. We can do Monday 5/17 10:30am PT for the alignment call.

Kira
Head of Platform, OptiScale
kira@optiscale.com

Date: 2027-05-12T12:20:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift

Team —

Forwarding OptiScale's clarifying questions and confirming the alignment call Monday 5/17 10:30am PT. Quick action items I think we should own before the call: 

- Marissa: can you produce a short two-column cost sheet (Essentials vs Premium) showing incremental cost as both per-token and per-hour for typical gen workloads? Include committed vs on-demand math.
- Ben: can you draft a burst-credit definition (hard caps, expiry, how it applies to overage billing) — target: <= 1 page.
- Monica: recommend an incident-credit formula linked to latency breach windows (e.g., credit = monthly recurring charge * breach-severity-weighted-duration / 720) with a worked example. Procurement wants deterministic language.
- Aditya: prep a one-slide ops-runbook outline and suggested canary cadence (10% -> 50% -> 100% over X days) and rollback criteria.

I moved the proposal to "redwood_sla_proposal_v2.pdf" and attached it to this thread. I also dropped a draft MPA redlines doc; procurement will want tracked changes.

Goal for Monday call: land on a preferred commercial track and agree two anchor items to surface in the MPA (credit formula and burst definition). If we can offer a modest concession (e.g., 10% off list for a 12-month commit + one month free burst credits) that may be sufficient to close without escalation.

Thanks —
Jordan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift

Jordan / team —

Quick notes ahead of Monday:

- Cost sheet: I'll surface committed hourly equivalents and the blended per-token delta. I recommend we show both the steady-state and a 30-day launch window with an assumed 3x traffic spike.
- Credit formula: Monica's suggestion looks good; suggest we cap max credit at 30% of monthly recurring bill to avoid runaway exposure.
- Tail SLO: OptiScale asked for 99.9th — recommend we offer 99.5th as a trade: tighter than standard, less risky to guarantee. Use canary to validate 99.9th before committing to it in MPA.
- Onboarding: propose a 4-week ops onboarding (week 1 discovery, week 2 canary and tuning, week 3 ramp, week 4 lessons & runbook handoff).

I'll be on the call Monday and can run the commercial worksheet live. If we want to present a firm sweetener, I'm comfortable with Jordan's suggested 10% for a 12-month commit + one month free burst credits on signing.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Renewal: governance, scaling, and crediting for SLA uplift — meeting summary & next steps

Kira / Jason —

Thanks for the productive call today. A few concrete outcomes and next steps: 

1) OptiScale indicated preference for the Premium Response track with a verification canary. We agreed to target 99.5th in the MPA and run a 30-day canary to validate 99.9th behavior before preserving it as a contractual SLO.
2) Commercials: Redwood will provide a 10% ARR discount for a 12-month commitment and one month (30 days) of burst credits (per the draft definition Ben will supply) applied at contract start.
3) Incident crediting: we agreed a deterministic formula (Monica will circulate language): credit = monthly recurring charge * min( breach_weighted_minutes / 720, 0.3 ). Cap at 30% of monthly bill.
4) DocuSign: I shared a DocuSign envelope (link below) with the redlined MPA reflecting the agreed items. Please have procurement review and provide countered changes by EOD Friday 5/21.

Immediate owners: Ben (burst def), Monica (incident credit clause), Marissa (commercial worksheet + onboarding schedule). I'll monitor HubSpot deal RDW-2027-OPT-1543 and move to Contract Review stage once we have counters.
